safety_verdicts.content: There is no evidence of cellulitis.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not state there is no cellulitis/no evidence of cellulitis.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failing to document that there was no evidence of cellulitis removes an important negative finding that helps justify conservative management and can serve as a baseline if symptoms worsen. This could contribute to later over-treatment (e.g., unnecessary antibiotics) or confusion about whether infection was already suspected.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Contradicts Gold ex-004 ('No rash seen on the arm') by asserting slight erythema.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting slight erythema when the reference source indicates no rash could shift interpretation toward a more significant local reaction or early infection, potentially prompting unnecessary monitoring or treatment. However, in the context of an insect sting, mild redness is common and this discrepancy is unlikely to cause substantial harm on its own.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Contradicts Gold ex-004 by describing the area as blotchy (implying a visible rash).

The most likely consequence is additional follow-up or unnecessary treatment rather than serious harm.
